findings.F1: In folds B and C, the tested situation does not give back the next day. Over all four folds the step-5 cases average -0.04 % unusual move (t -0.19, 655 cases, 331 days). In the visible folds the 237 `trending` cases average -0.64 % next-day unusual move (t -1.60), which is not significant and points away from what folds A and D must hold.
findings.F2: Inside the tested regime, the moderate rises fade and the largest do not, which is the opposite of the claimed grading. Rises of 1 to 2 swing units average -1.07 % the next day (t -2.14, 160 cases). Rises above 2 swing units average -0.66 % (t -0.86, 43 cases).
findings.F3: In falling markets (60-day return below -10 %), rises of 1 to 2 swing units average -4.15 % over the next 3 days (t -2.53, 56 cases), and -5.50 % when calm (t -2.42, 33 cases). The same cases on the two other 3-day grids give only -0.98 % (t -0.81) and -0.47 % (t -0.24). The result depends on where the grid starts, so it is not a robust effect.
findings.F4: The 3-day fade after falling-market rises above 1 swing unit reverses in 2021 (+3.66 %, t 1.03, 18 cases) after 2018 to 2020 (-3.2 % to -6.2 %, t -1.27 to -1.85). No single year reaches t 2.
findings.F5: The other angles show nothing that stands out once the number of looks is counted:
findings.F6: The idea's move per case is -0.17 % in total and -0.04 % unusual, against a 0.22 % cost per trade. Even F2's -1.07 % on a subset would be a small, uncertain margin over cost.

no_ideas: I looked at the forecast's grading, the tested regime by range-close and size, falling and choppy markets by scaled-return bucket at 1 to 5 days on every grid offset, calm against agitated, years, coins and weekdays, and the only patterns that pass t 2 either change with the grid's starting bar or are what chance gives over that many looks (F3, F5), so none stands out enough to be a finding to build an idea on.
